title: Vicente Fox Presidency Update — Sep 15, 2026
summary: Three new post-presidential events added covering Fox's activity from late August through early September 2026. On August 25, Fox escalated his defense of detained former Baja California governor Ernesto Ruffo Appel, alleging psychological mistreatment at the Altiplano federal prison. On September 4, Fox visited PRI national headquarters to meet party leader Alejandro 'Alito' Moreno and PRI executives — his most visible engagement yet with the party his 2000 victory unseated — to explore a citizen-led opposition front via his 'Alma de México' platform ahead of the 2027 midterms. The next day, Fox addressed over 5,000 PAN youth in Aguascalientes, calling for opposition unity to 'partirle la madre a Morena' in 2027; President Sheinbaum dismissed the overture as a return to the past. New map points were added for the Altiplano prison, PRI headquarters, and the Aguascalientes venue, and two new political figures (Alejandro Moreno, Ernesto Ruffo Appel) were added to the political roster.

summary: Four new post-presidential events added covering Fox's activity from late July through mid-August 2026. title: Vicente Fox Presidency Update — Jul 16, 2026
summary: Four new post-presidential events added covering Fox's activity from late May through mid-July 2026. Fox and Calderón rallied behind Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos at a PAN event on May 30, branding Morena a 'perfect dictatorship' and accusing the federal government of shielding Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya. On June 1, Fox criticized federal 'Bienestar' welfare programs as wasteful, contrasting them with his own targeted Oportunidades program. A June 24 home interview for YouTube's Café Ciudadano saw Fox call AMLO 'stubborn' and Sheinbaum 'communist, not scientific,' drawing sharp Morena backlash. Most significantly, Centro Fox — the presidential library and leadership center Fox built at his San Cristóbal ranch in 2007 — closed after 18 years on July 9, its facilities ceded to Universidad Incarnate Word (Texas) under a 100-year agreement, marking a symbolic end-of-cycle moment for his post-presidential legacy project. The San Cristóbal map point has been updated to reflect the closure.
